description: In defk-9vl, kernels whose generated C and machine code were identical to main (only at different addresses) swung about ±3% between builds (count_primes yielding 177 vs 180-182 ms, count_primes_via_call the opposite way). That noise is the same size as effects we try to measure. Options: try -falign-loops / -falign-functions in the NIF build, or have benches report a spread across several builds (e.g. perturb layout) instead of one best-of. Done when a ±3% claim can be told apart from layout noise.

comments.text: Triage (defk-sgw plan): ready-for-human. Measurement work that needs a quiet machine and judgement about noise.

2026-10-26 (owner): option 1 first: bench/layout_noise.exs builds one kernel several times with only its code layout moved (padding before it), interleaved like bench/float_checks.exs, reports median and range; docs/performance.md 1.7 gets the rule that a difference inside that range is noise. The -falign-* flag experiment is a follow-up ticket, measured with this band.

PR #84 (branch defk-wnu/layout-noise-band, worktree ../defk-wnu). Quiet run 2026-10-26, 15 rounds: integer loops layout range 2.9-3.6% vs A/A control 0.2-2.1%; sum/dot 1.2-1.9%, near control. mix ci passed. Close after merge; defk-w8r.4 then unblocks.

title: Make code-layout timing noise visible or stable
